title: Yakisoba (Japanese Fried Noodles with Chicken and Cabbage)
summary: Japanese fried noodles tossed with chicken and cabbage in a sweet-savoury sauce built on Worcestershire sauce, ketchup and soy.
equipment: wok (35 cm) or large non-stick frying pan (30 cm)
small bowls for the prepared ingredients

ingredients.item: skinless chicken thigh fillets, thinly sliced
carrot, thinly sliced on an angle
white or napa cabbage, in 2 cm strips
spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Stir together the Worcestershire sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar in a small bowl. This distinctive blend is what gives yakisoba its familiar tangy-sweet flavour, quite different from a typical soy-based stir-fry sauce.

steps.title: Loosen the noodles
steps.text: Run the noodles under hot water for 1 minute, then shake them dry. Packaged yakisoba noodles are already cooked, so this step simply separates the strands without softening them any further.

steps.title: Char the vegetables
steps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in the wok over high heat and stir-fry the onion, carrot and shiitake for 2-3 minutes until spotty brown, then add the cabbage and spring onions and cook for a further 2-3 minutes, leaving everything to sit still between stirs so it chars in places while staying crisp. Letting the vegetables rest against the hot metal rather than stirring constantly is what gives them those browned, flavourful edges.

steps.title: Sear and cook the chicken
steps.text: Lift the vegetables out, add 1 tablespoon of oil and spread the chicken in a single layer, searing for 1 minute before stirring and cooking for a further 3-4 minutes until browned all over with no pink remaining and it reaches 74°C at the thickest piece. Searing it first in one layer rather than stirring immediately helps it brown rather than steam in its own moisture.

steps.title: Fry the noodles
steps.text: Add the remaining oil and the loosened noodles to the wok and fry for 1-2 minutes to heat them through and pick up a little colour. This brief fry on their own lets the noodles start to crisp slightly before the sauce goes in.

steps.title: Sauce the noodles
steps.text: Pour in the sauce and water and toss everything, scraping the base of the wok, until the noodles are evenly coated and hot throughout. Scraping the pan as you toss lifts any sauce that's caught on the bottom, so nothing gets left behind.

steps.title: Combine and serve
steps.text: Return the charred vegetables to the wok and toss for 1 minute until everything is well mixed and evenly coloured. Serve topped with pickled red ginger and aonori, if using.

tips: Let the vegetables sit against the hot wok between stirs instead of moving them constantly — that stillness is what gives yakisoba its characteristic charred edges.
Cook the chicken in a single layer and sear before stirring; crowding or stirring too soon steams it instead of browning it.
Rinse the noodles just to loosen them, not to warm them through fully — they finish heating in the wok, and over-rinsing can make them waterlogged.
Add the sauce gradually while scraping the pan so it coats evenly rather than pooling at the bottom under the noodles.
storage: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot pan or wok with a splash of water until piping hot (74°C) throughout; the noodles can turn a little soft if reheated in a microwave, so a quick pan-fry works better. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
